title: Slice P: Node>=24 bundled package and tag-driven release-readiness (DEC-299)
description:
glyph 0.1.0 packaging (DEC-299 item 2 and 3). Target Node >=24 like lore and quest: one bundled dist/glyph.js with a node shebang, bin glyph, files [dist, README.md, LICENSE], engines node >=24. Bun.spawnSync (src/git.ts, src/codemap.ts) replaced by node:child_process spawnSync behind one helper. Development and tests stay on Bun. private is removed and version set to 0.1.0 only in the release change, not in this slice. Independent of Slice S. Floor work (CI and release): Opus review before landing.

ROUTE PRECEDENT (read by ref 2026-11-22): lore-cli .github/workflows/release.yml and quest-cli .github/workflows/release.yml both publish by npm OIDC Trusted Publishing (id-token: write, environment release, node 24, npm@^11 with an asserted OIDC floor, one-time npmjs.com Trusted Publisher setup per package); both are human-triggered (workflow_dispatch against a v* tag, publish input defaulting false) rather than fired by a tag push. DEC-299 says tag-driven with provenance on DEC-240 terms (npm install --ignore-scripts at exact versions, checkout persist-credentials false, no interpolated step outputs in run). The implementer must re-read both workflows and the quest history (DEC-299 notes release.yml had never succeeded for quest and local publish scripts were the working precedent) before choosing, and record the route in the task. Any route keeps npm publish itself an operator step.

OPERATOR TIER-3 CHECKLIST (the operator takes these directly; never agent steps, never relayed):
- [ ] configure the npmjs.com Trusted Publisher for @opum-ai/glyph (repository, workflow filename, environment)
- [ ] npm publish of @opum-ai/glyph 0.1.0 (dispatch or tag as the route defines)
- [ ] flip opum-ai/glyph-cli from private to public

acceptanceCriteria.text: package.json has bin { glyph: dist/glyph.js }, files exactly [dist, README.md, LICENSE], engines node >=24, and a build script producing one bundled dist/glyph.js beginning with a node shebang (proof: a test reads package.json and the built file head; npm pack --dry-run lists only those paths)
a LICENSE file exists at the repo root and is included in the tarball (proof: npm pack --dry-run listing in CI)

no Bun global remains in shipped source: Bun.spawnSync is replaced by node:child_process spawnSync behind exactly one helper used by src/git.ts and src/codemap.ts (proof: grep of src/ for Bun. returns nothing outside the helper-free tree, and the full test suite still passes under Bun)
development and tests still run on Bun (proof: bun test, typecheck, lint and format:check remain green in the Check job)

CI packs the tarball, installs it into an empty directory, and runs glyph under node (not bun) for every command in the manifest, asserting each exits with its expected code (proof: a CI step whose command list is generated from help --json so a new command without coverage fails it)
CI fails when dist is missing from the packed tarball (proof: a negative run on a tarball built with dist removed exits non-zero, shown in the same job or a recorded run)

the release workflow is tag-driven with npm provenance and satisfies DEC-240 (install with --ignore-scripts at exact versions, checkout persist-credentials false, no step output interpolated in run, Quest version read inside the managed markers) and the chosen route and its rationale against lore and quest precedent are recorded in the task (proof: workflow file review by Opus and an actionlint or equivalent clean run)
a publish dry run (publish false) runs end to end in CI without publishing and shows provenance would be attached (proof: a recorded run id and the npm publish --dry-run --provenance log)
private stays true and version stays 0.0.0 in this slice (proof: package.json diff)
the operator tier-3 checklist is present in this task and none of its items is performed or relayed by an agent (proof: the checklist items remain unchecked until the operator reports)
